name: When should I stain or restain the interior logs of my home?

mainEntity.name: When should I stain or restain the interior logs of my home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Interior log staining is typically done to change the wood tone, seal the timber, or refresh aged, darkened surfaces. Unlike exterior logs that face direct UV rays and driving rain, interior logs mainly suffer from dust, cooking oils, grease, and indoor light discoloration. You should consider restaining if the existing clear coat has turned amber or cloudy, if the logs look dry, or during a broader cabin renovation when you want a uniform shade across rooms. Before proceeding, assess whether you just need a deep cleaning or a full sand and restain, as heavy grease near kitchens requires degreasing before any finish will adhere properly.
acceptedAnswer.description: Stain interior logs to update wood tone, correct yellowing finishes, or protect bare timber from dust and moisture. They only need restaining every 10 to 15+ years unless cosmetically dated.
